item.title: The wrong platform for science | Science
item.description: Daniel Blumstein recently sat in a Colorado meadow waiting for yellow-bellied marmots to appear, as the ecologist and evolutionary biologist had done many times before, the New York Times reported. But on this occasion, he was also preoccupied by news of dramatic cuts to federal research funding. As Blumstein made observations contributing to his study of the evolution of mammalian sociality, his mind turned to an idea from the television adaptation of the novel Margo’s Got Money Troubles; in the series, a young single mother, unable to find work, turns to OnlyFans, a social media platform used primarily, though not exclusively, to share adult content.

item.title: Wars exacerbate the biodiversity crisis | Science
item.description: Wars harm species and ecosystems and erode biodiversity conservation institutions and support. Given that environmental protection is essential for long-term peace and security, biodiversity conservation should not be abandoned in times of crisis. Scientists and the international community should work to monitor ecological damage and incorporate conservation into diplomatic resolutions to conflicts.

item.title: Fencing threatens China’s protected areas | Science
item.description: In recent years, large-scale blade razor wire isolation fences have been erected in many of China’s iconic scenic areas and nature reserves, triggering widespread public and academic debate (1, 2). Although such hard barrier facilities effectively reduce illegal tourism behaviors and simplify scenic area management, their ecological consequences for mountain forest ecosystems have been largely ignored.
